results.claim: There is an explicit packing of 518 A10 rectangles in one A1 rectangle.
results.proof_sketch: Use container [0,594]×[0,841]. Place A_{i,j}=[37i,37(i+1)]×[26j,26(j+1)] for 0≤i<2, 0≤j<32 (64 rectangles). Place B_i=[74+37i,74+37(i+1)]×[0,26] for 0≤i<14 (14 rectangles). Finally place C_{i,j}=[74+26i,74+26(i+1)]×[26+37j,26+37(j+1)] for 0≤i<20, 0≤j<22 (440 rectangles). The three families occupy respectively [0,74]×[0,832], [74,592]×[0,26], and [74,594]×[26,840], so they are contained and have disjoint interiors. Their total size is 64+14+440=518.

results.claim: No packing can contain 519 A10 rectangles; a ten-residue periodic marker certificate gives the upper bound 518.
results.proof_sketch:
First reduce real coordinates to integers rigorously. Fix the rectangles' vertical coordinates and orientations and minimize the sum of their horizontal coordinates over the nonempty compact feasible set. At a minimizer, every rectangle not at x=0 has a left blocker whose vertical interior overlaps it; otherwise a sufficiently small left shift would lower the sum. Following blockers strictly decreases x and ends at x=0, so every x-coordinate is a sum of integral widths. Holding these integral x-coordinates fixed and minimizing the sum of y-coordinates gives integral y-coordinates analogously.

Now mark unit cell (x,y) when (x mod 37,y mod 37) lies in P={(3,3),(7,25),(10,14),(14,7),(18,29),(22,11),(25,33),(29,22),(33,36),(36,18)}. Exact enumeration of all 37 cyclic starts shows that every length-26 interval contains 7 or 8 selected first-coordinate residues and 7 or 8 selected second-coordinate residues. Hence either orientation of an integer-positioned A10 rectangle contains at least seven marks. Since 594=16·37+2 and no selected first residue is 0 or 1, every selected first residue occurs in 16 container columns. Since 841=22·37+27, seven selected second residues occur in 23 rows and three in 22 rows. Thus the container has 16(7·23+3·22)=3632 marks. Disjoint rectangles cover disjoint unit cells, whereas 519 rectangles require at least 7·519=3633 marks. Therefore at most 518 fit.

final_writeup:
The recorded 258-versus-259 dichotomy is false for the literal ISO dimensions supplied in the target. An A10 sheet is 26×37 mm and an A1 sheet is 594×841 mm; the exact orthogonal packing number is

OPT(594,841,37,26)=518.

For the lower bound, tile [0,74]×[0,832] with a 2×32 grid of 37×26 rectangles, place fourteen further 37×26 rectangles in [74,592]×[0,26], and tile [74,594]×[26,840] with a 20×22 grid of 26×37 rectangles. The blocks have disjoint interiors and contain 64+14+440=518 rectangles. Exact unit-cell verification finds 498316=518·37·26 occupied cells and 1238 uncovered cells.

For the upper bound, arbitrary real coordinates may first be replaced by integer coordinates without changing cardinality. With vertical coordinates fixed, minimize the sum of horizontal coordinates over the compact feasible set. Every rectangle away from x=0 then has a left-touching blocker; a blocker chain strictly decreases x until reaching x=0, expressing every x-coordinate as a sum of the integral rectangle widths. Fixing those x-coordinates and applying the same compact-minimization argument vertically makes every y-coordinate integral.

For integer placements, mark a unit cell when its coordinate pair modulo 37 belongs to

P={(3,3),(7,25),(10,14),(14,7),(18,29),(22,11),(25,33),(29,22),(33,36),(36,18)}.

Checking the 37 possible cyclic starts shows that every interval of 26 residues contains seven or eight selected first coordinates and seven or eight selected second coordinates. A 37×26 or 26×37 rectangle therefore contains at least seven marked cells. In the container, each selected first residue occurs in 16 columns. Seven selected second residues occur in 23 rows and three occur in 22 rows, giving exactly

16(7·23+3·22)=3632

marked cells. Any 519 pairwise interior-disjoint rectangles would cover at least 7·519=3633 distinct marked cells, an impossibility. Thus 518 is both attainable and optimal. The exact checker independently examined all 455328 integer placements of size 37×26 and all 458045 placements of size 26×37; every placement contained seven or eight marks.

Consequently neither 258 nor 259 is correct for the literal A10-in-A1 problem, and the stronger exact result fully resolves the target.
